chapter.title: Mineral Fuels, Mineral Oils and Products of Their Distillation; Bituminous Substances; Mineral Waxes

page.h1: HTS Chapter 27: Mineral Fuels, Mineral Oils and Products of Their Distillation; Bituminous Substances; Mineral Waxes — Export Markets & Foreign Tariffs on U.S. Goods

seo.title: Chapter 27 Export Markets: Tariffs on U.S. Energy by Country
seo.shortDescription: The tariff each top buyer charges on U.S. crude oil, refined fuels, LNG and coal, with the trade agreement and energy regulator for each.

intro: The largest buyers charge little or nothing on crude oil, LNG and coal: the EU is duty-free on all three and Mexico and Canada charge nothing under USMCA. Rates for South Korea, Japan, India, Brazil, the United Kingdom and Taiwan were not confirmed from an official 2026 schedule, so those cells say so rather than guess. China, no longer a top-nine buyer, is the one market with a heavy tariff on U.S. energy. For LNG into the EU, the rule that matters most is not a tariff but the EU's methane regulation, which will require importers to show their suppliers meet EU methane monitoring standards.
valueBasis: FOB value of U.S. exports, as reported by the United States to UN Comtrade.

assumptions: Rates come from the trade agreements (USMCA, CUSMA) and, for the EU, Japan, India and the others, from each market's customs tariff where it could be confirmed. Where an official 2026 figure was not found, the cell says 'not individually verified' rather than showing a guess.

Four headings carry nearly the whole chapter (refined fuels 2710, crude oil 2709, natural gas and LNG 2711, coal 2701). The other 12 headings are under 6% together and are shown with the market-wide default.

Energy duties are often set by use (for example refined fuels for refining or chemical use can be duty-free in the EU), so the EU rate for refined fuels is shown as a range and should be confirmed on the exact TARIC line.
Fuel excise and petroleum taxes (for example Japan's petroleum and coal tax, India's cess) are domestic taxes, not tariffs, and are not shown.
National 8–10-digit tariff lines can set a different rate than the four-digit group shown here — check the market's own schedule before relying on this page for a transaction.
